summary:
**Helios – Explore the Universe, Understand Our Place in It**

Helios is an interactive space exploration platform designed to make the wonders of our universe more accessible, visual, and engaging. We developed a browser-based space simulation experience where users can explore different celestial objects, from the planets in our Solar System to distant exoplanets and galaxies, through detailed 4K visualizations.

Our goal was to bring space exploration beyond ordinary images and information by creating an experience where people can visually discover celestial objects and learn about them along the way. By combining interactive visual models with astronomical facts and descriptions, Helios helps bridge the gap between complex scientific information and the curiosity of everyday explorers.

We believe understanding the universe should be exciting and accessible to everyone. Helios aims to inspire curiosity, encourage learning, and help people develop a deeper appreciation of the cosmos. It is more than just exploring space; it is about inspiring people to ask questions, discover new worlds, and understand the universe we are part of.
details:
**Helios – Exploring the Universe, One World at a Time**

Helios is a space exploration project built around one simple idea: making the wonders of our universe easier to explore, understand, and appreciate.

Space is incredibly fascinating, but understanding planets, stars, galaxies, and distant planetary systems can sometimes feel complicated, especially when information is scattered across different websites and resources. We wanted to create an experience that brings these wonders closer to people through an engaging and visually immersive interface.

With Helios, our goal is to turn learning about space into something more than just reading facts. We want people to feel curious, explore different celestial objects, discover planetary systems, and develop a deeper appreciation for the universe around us.

**How does it work?**

Helios brings together visual representations of celestial objects and astronomical information in an interactive space exploration experience. The project focuses on planets, stars, galaxies, and planetary systems, allowing users to explore and learn about different objects in the universe.

We referred to NASA's Eyes (eyes.nasa.gov) throughout development to understand planetary models, planetary systems, and astronomical representations. This helped us make our visualizations more meaningful and keep our work connected to actual astronomical references.

**What makes Helios special?**

One of the things we really wanted to achieve with Helios was to make space exploration feel exciting rather than overwhelming. Instead of presenting astronomy as a collection of complicated scientific terms, we focused on creating a visually engaging experience that encourages people to explore out of curiosity.

We also paid attention to the appearance of individual celestial objects, because every planet, star, and galaxy has its own characteristics. We wanted our visual representations to reflect these differences as closely as possible while maintaining an immersive and consistent visual experience.

**Tools and Technologies Used**

We used a combination of AI-assisted tools, development platforms, and NASA resources throughout the project:

- **Antigravity:** Used as our primary development environment to build and develop the overall Helios user interface.

- **ChatGPT:** Assisted us with developing planetary and astronomical visual concepts, researching ideas, and refining different aspects of the project.

- **Claude:** Helped us with additional planetary and galaxy-related visual development and creative refinement.

- **NASA Eyes (eyes.nasa.gov):** Served as an important reference for studying planetary models, planetary systems, and the representation of celestial objects.

AI tools played a supporting role in our development process, helping us experiment with ideas, overcome creative challenges, and bring our vision closer to reality. The overall direction, selection of visual elements, project concept, and integration of these elements into Helios were guided by our own decisions.

**Intended Impact**

We hope Helios can make people more interested in astronomy and encourage them to explore questions about the universe. Whether someone is a student discovering space for the first time or simply someone fascinated by the stars, we want Helios to provide an enjoyable starting point for learning.

We believe that technology can make scientific exploration more accessible, and Helios is our attempt to combine creativity, technology, and astronomy into one experience.

**Our Vision**

Helios is more than just a project about planets and stars. It represents our curiosity about the universe and our desire to make that curiosity accessible to others. There is so much beyond our own planet that we have yet to understand, and we hope Helios inspires people to look beyond Earth and explore the incredible universe we are part of.
